newsitem.title: USA: Mexican drug lord may be extradited to U.S.-paper.
newsitem.headline: Mexican drug lord may be extradited to U.S.-paper.

text.p: Jailed Mexican drug kingpin Oscar Malherbe de Leon may be extradited to the United States next month for trial on drug-trafficking charges, a newspaper reported on Friday.
The Houston Chronicle, quoting unnamed sources, said drug agents here hoped to use Malherbe to get more information about Mexico's top drug-trafficker, Amado Carrillo Fuentes.
It said Malhberbe had forged an alliance with Carrillo Fuentes, known as "The Lord of the Skies," after taking charge of the Gulf drug cartel based in northern Mexico.
Malherbe, 34, reportedly became chief of the Gulf cartel after its leader Juan Garcia Abrego was arrested in January 1996 in Monterrey, Mexico and flown to the United States for trial.
Malherbe was arrested on drug charges on February 26 in Mexico City. Shortly thereafter, U.S. officials requested his extradition here to face charges from an indictment first issued in 1993.

The Mexican government traditionally has resisted extraditing its citizens, but Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo, during President Bill Clinton's visit to Mexico last month, said it would be considered in special cases.
The Chronicle said a U.S. State Department spokesman would not comment on Malherbe's status.

Garcia Abrego was convicted on drug charges in a Houston trial last fall and sentenced to life in prison without parole. Technically, he was expelled from Mexico to the United States, not extradited, because he supposedly was a U.S. citizen.
